skill.name: skill-check
skill.description: Tests and audits Agent Skills for structure, security, eval coverage, script behavior, I/O contracts, and best-practice compliance.
skill.summary: Audit Agent Skills with structured static, functional, security, and quality checks.
skill.author: JckJhns

security_audit.summary: Most static pattern hits are documentation examples, Markdown formatting, or deliberately unsafe eval fixtures rather than active malicious code. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files. Two semantic risks remain: target script execution in Standard and Deep checks, and unpinned pip installation guidance using --break-system-packages.

remediation.issue: Untrusted target scripts can be executed during Standard and Deep checks.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before every target script execution, run scripts in a sandbox, and disable network access unless requested.

remediation.issue: Mock dependency guidance installs packages with --break-system-packages.
remediation.suggestion: Use a virtual environment, pin package versions, avoid --break-system-packages, and ask before installing any dependency.

remediation.issue: Dangerous fixture scripts are bundled as normal Python files under evals.
remediation.suggestion: Keep insecure fixtures clearly labeled, do not execute them in evals, and add guard comments near each dangerous function.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Target Script Execution
semantic_findings.description: Standard and Deep workflows instruct the agent to execute scripts from the skill being tested after static review. This can run untrusted code from a user-selected skill directory if the review misses a dangerous pattern.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly runs scripts from the target skill and only requires a warning when Critical findings were detected. This is a real execution risk for untrusted skills, although it supports the testing purpose.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Installation With System Package Override
semantic_findings.description: Mock generation guidance tells the agent to install third-party packages with pip and --break-system-packages when binary formats are needed. This can modify the host Python environment and exposes users to dependency supply-chain risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dependency section directly recommends pip install commands without pinning, hashes, virtual environments, or mandatory user confirmation. The --break-system-packages flag increases the environment modification risk.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need reliable evidence before sharing a skill. SkillCheck guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured audits, eval checks, and security review.
actual_capabilities: Runs Quick, Standard, and Deep audit workflows for Agent Skills.
Checks SKILL.md metadata, references, assets, scripts, and eval files.
Compares script invocations against actual script arguments.
Reviews bundled scripts and instructions for security risks.
Generates mock inputs for functional and I/O contract testing.
Produces structured reports with findings, evidence, and recommendations.
limitations: Standard and Deep workflows may execute scripts from the skill under test.
Some binary mock files need optional Python packages.
Security review is guidance-based and can miss novel malicious behavior.
Subjective output quality checks still require reviewer judgment.

use_cases.title: Validate a New Skill
use_cases.description: Run a release check before uploading or publishing a custom Agent Skill.

use_cases.title: Review a Community Skill
use_cases.description: Inspect structure, scripts, and security risks before installing an unfamiliar skill.

use_cases.title: Regression Test Skill Changes
use_cases.description: Use existing evals and generated tests to catch behavior changes after edits.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Quick Check on the skill in this folder and report the main issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Specific Skill Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the Agent Skill at <skill-path>. Focus on metadata, references, scripts, and security risks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Standard Functional Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Standard Check on <skill-path>. Show the test plan before executing any bundled scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Perform Deep Release Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Deep Check on <skill-path>. Include edge cases, eval regression, script behavior, and release recommendations.

output_examples.input: Run a Quick Check on a chart-generation skill.
output: Summary verdict with passed and failed checks.
Security section listing any risky scripts or instructions.
Best-practice score with the most important fixes.

output_examples.input: Run a Standard Check on a skill with one Python script.
output: Test plan for static checks, eval regression, script tests, and I/O tests.
Execution results with stdout, stderr, exit status, and generated file checks.
Recommendations ordered by security and functional impact.
Progress report that separates finished parts from missing parts.
Specific next steps for placeholders, missing files, and unclear outputs.

best_practices: Start with Quick Check before running any target skill scripts.
Review the proposed Standard or Deep test plan before execution.
Run script and dependency tests in a sandbox when reviewing community skills.
anti_patterns: Do not execute target scripts before reading the security findings.
Do not treat the best-practice score as the whole release verdict.
Do not ignore cross-reference mismatches between SKILL.md and scripts.

faq.question: What does SkillCheck test?
faq.answer: It checks skill structure, references, scripts, evals, security risks, I/O contracts, and best practices.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it execute code?
faq.answer: Quick Check does not execute target scripts. Standard and Deep checks can execute scripts after review.

faq.question: Can it prove a skill is secure?
faq.answer: No. It helps find common risks, but reviewers should still inspect high-risk code manually.

faq.question: When should I use Deep Check?
faq.answer: Use Deep Check before broad distribution or when you need edge-case and workflow coverage.

faq.question: Does it create new skills?
faq.answer: No. SkillCheck tests existing skills. Use a separate authoring workflow to create or edit skills.
